title: Your First CLI Tool
description: Node.js + Claude API. Build a command-line tool that does something useful.

title: Arguments & Options
description: User input handling. Let people control your tool with flags and arguments.

title: Deploy as an npm Package
description: Publish to npm. Make your tool globally installable and shareable.

title: Add Complexity
description: Multi-step workflows, file I/O, configuration files. Make it production-ready.

title: Config Files & Secrets
description: Stop hardcoding values. Manage settings and API keys the right way.

title: Designing a CLI People Won't Fight
description: Design a command-line interface with a command structure that matches how it's actually used, flags with defaults that need no manual, help text people read instead of skip, output that survives a pipe, and interactive prompts that know when to get out of the way.

title: State, Config and Secrets
description: Manage a CLI tool's configuration and credentials without embarrassing yourself: choosing the right OS-conventional home for state, a config format and precedence order that don't surprise anyone, environment variables used for what they're actually good at, a credential that isn't sitting in plaintext everywhere, and a config migration that doesn't break the users you already have.

title: Errors, Exit Codes and Scriptability
description: Make a CLI tool safe to script around by other programs, not just run by hand: exit codes chosen on purpose, error messages aimed at the person actually reading them, a machine-readable mode that's explicit rather than inferred, batch failures that don't hide behind a false success, and tests that call the real binary the way a script would.

title: Packaging and Distribution
description: Get a CLI tool onto someone else's machine with one command: knowing what a stranger's install actually needs, publishing to npm with a version and file list that don't surprise anyone, the cross-platform gotchas that only show up off your own machine, an honest answer to whether the tool needs auto-update at all, and an install section nobody gets stuck on.

title: Putting AI Inside a CLI Tool
description: Use an AI step inside a command-line tool without making it slow, expensive or flaky: deciding where a network call belongs in a fast local tool, streaming so the terminal doesn't feel frozen, caching responses for a tool people run repeatedly, falling back gracefully when the API is unavailable, and keeping cost predictable before a batch job runs, not after the bill arrives.
